description:
Customer Success Manager

🌍 About us

Plinth is a fast-growing tech startup working with charities, foundations and local government. Small and local charities are highly effective but largely hidden. They have no spare time and no spare money. We're building the tools these organisations need and shining a light on the work they do. Read more on our blog.

🚀We're growing fast. 3-4x this year. We get 7+ new clients a month and we're shipping new features every few days. This means things move quickly and your work directly shapes how we scale. You'll have real responsibility from day one.

❤️It's really impactful work. Our clients are charities and grassroots organisations across the UK, and soon internationally. When you help them succeed with our platform, you're directly amplifying their impact. Every successful onboarding means a charity spends less time fighting with their systems and more time on their actual mission.

🤝You'll work with impressive people. Our team is talented, collaborative and slightly strange(?). We value impact, speed and openness. We work in person in our office in Old Street because we genuinely enjoy each other's company (most of the time). It’s a high trust, creative space where if you think something's a good idea, you just go do it.

💼 You need to be able to:

  • Work both fast and slow: You'll navigate slow public sector procurement cycles one minute, then help us ship a new feature over lunch the next. The whiplash is intense but it keeps things interesting.

  • Keep it real: You'll be getting the train to community centres and youth clubs where the heating doesn't work and where the paint is peeling off the walls. It’s rarely glamourous. You need to be willing to meet clients where they are, literally and figuratively.

  • Listen to problems, ignore solutions: Clients will tell you exactly what they think they need. Your job is to understand the actual problem and guide them to what will really work, even when they're convinced they already know the answer. This requires self-confidence, understanding of the platform and genuine listening in equal measure.

  • Teach people: Most of our clients don't love shiny gadgets. If you're the kind of person who enjoys teaching your gran to use a smartphone, this is ideal. You need to explain some fairly complex systems clearly without being condescending and still getting user adoption

  • Automate and document yourself away:🤖 We're small and growing fast. Build systems and processes that make your job increasingly redundant. There’s always plenty more to do.

  • Understand the difference between "urgent" and 🚨 URGENT — When you're managing 4-8 concurrent client projects and everyone thinks their issue is critical, you need to distinguish between what must happen for launch versus what can wait. This is harder than it sounds.

  • Grow with the role: we need someone who is comfortable with our clients and team doubling every 6 months. Your role will rapidly change to reflect that, but it leaves you with lots of room to grow in responsibility.

🧩 What kind of background do we think would be a good fit?

We’d expect a few years experience in something like the following:

  • Coaching / Tutoring: You know how to meet people where they are and guide them to better outcomes

  • Hospitality management: Service mindset, de-escalation skills, managing expectations when things don't go to plan, letting the customer think they’re right when they aren’t

  • Event/production management: Used to juggling moving pieces, keeping stakeholders calm, making last-minute pivots when things go wrong

  • Community organising/activism: Already comfortable in the spaces you'll be visiting, get the mission, used to working with limited resources

  • Consulting: You're used to parachuting into chaos, extracting actionable tasks, and keeping multiple clients calm simultaneously

  • User research/UX: Good at understanding what people actually need versus what they say they need, synthesising feedback into actionable insights

  • Knowledge of the charity sector is a significant advantage, whether that’s as an employee, consultant or as a long term volunteer.

  • It would also definitely be helpful if you have any technical experience to help with managing data migrations.

Importantly, This is a list of suggestions.

If you have experience in only some of this, or have only some of these skills, please do apply anyway.

📈 How can you measure your success?

  • Speed of getting customers successfully using Plinth: From signed contract to actively using the platform and seeing value.

  • Positive recommendations: Clients recommending us positively to their networks — it’s a big source of our growth.

  • Increasing use of Plinth: Clients expanding how they use the platform over time, not just maintaining baseline usage

🧠 The role

Client Onboarding (70%) — Lead onboarding from kick-off to go-live. Break down complex projects into clear phases. Manage timelines, priorities, and expectations across 7+ new clients per month. Stay on top of new features we ship every few days. Push back when needed and teach anyone regardless of background.

Operations & Process Improvement (30%) — Audit and optimise our support systems (expect to manage Intercom chat a couple of days a week). Refine onboarding workflows. Keep documentation current. Work with engineering to communicate what's urgent versus what's just a problem. Track feature requests across clients and synthesise them into product improvements.

💵 What we offer

  • Salary: £42,000 - £75,000 depending on experience

  • Equity as part of your package

  • Location: In-person, Old Street, London

☎️ Interview process

  1. Quick (20-30 min) call with Chris as a sanity check

  2. First interview with Chris and a co-founder

  3. Long (2-3 hour), quite intense, in-person interview — meet the team, do tasks, respond to case studies, be challenged

  4. Decision

description:
TLDR: Plinth builds software for charities, foundations and funders. 2,000+ UK organisations use us, we add 7+ clients a month, and we ship constantly. HR, security, legal and finance currently sit with one person. That stops working at our next size. We're hiring someone to own a chunk of it: recruitment operations, contracts and invoicing, and the paperwork behind our ISO 27001 certification. You don't need to have done security or legal work before. You need to be the kind of person who picks up something unfamiliar, works out how it should run, then runs it properly.

What you'll own

  • Recruitment operations. The pipeline end to end. Keeping our tools current, booking interviews, wrangling schedules, first-pass CV screening, and working with team leads to build the tasks candidates get set. Candidates never wait on us

  • Contracting and invoicing. Contracts out, chased, signed and filed. Invoices raised and paid. Unglamorous, and it matters that someone holds it

  • Security administration. We're going through ISO 27001 now, and keeping a certification is more work than getting one. Reviews on a schedule, evidence that has to exist, paperwork that has to be generated. You own that calendar and it doesn't slip

  • Security questionnaires. Customers send long ones and they hold up deals. You'll answer them with support from the team and our internal tooling, and build a reusable answer bank so the tenth takes an hour instead of a day. You don't need to be a security expert. You do need to be confident enough to learn out loud

  • Automating the repeatable bits. A lot of this job is the same task on a loop, and a lot of it shouldn't be. Doing something by hand for the tenth time is a bug you're responsible for. You'll build the templates, automations and AI workflows that take it off your plate, then move on to harder work

  • Making the role bigger. Ops is four functions and one and a half people. As we grow, you're first in line for whatever you've shown you can hold

What we're looking for

  • You're the organiser. The one who books the group holiday, runs the spreadsheet and gets everyone to actually pay. That instinct is most of this job

  • You'll have a go at unfamiliar work. We'll hand you a contract, a security review, or a process nobody has written down. You won't be on your own with it, but we need someone whose instinct is to attempt it, ask a colleague to check it, and be better at it next time, rather than wait to be shown

  • You've probably done this shape of job. EA, team assistant, ops coordinator, office manager, practice manager. Somewhere you were the reliable centre of a lot of moving parts

  • Nothing gets quietly dropped. Interviews, invoices, an ISO review and a half-finished questionnaire, all live at once, none of them missing

  • You write clearly and fast. To candidates, to customers' IT teams, to a lawyer. Warm, plain, no waffle

  • Discretion. You'll be close to salary data, contracts and personal information from day one

  • You use AI properly. You've used Claude or similar beyond chatting: drafting, summarising, first passes at questionnaires, small workflows you built yourself. If you've touched Claude Code or automation tools, say so. It's how a small ops team keeps up with a company doubling every six months

Nice to have

  • Exposure to ISO 27001, SOC 2 or Cyber Essentials, from any angle

  • Experience with recruitment

  • Experience with contracts, procurement or finance admin

  • Charity, funder or local government background

What good looks like after a year

  • Recruitment runs without the Chief of Staff touching the logistics

  • ISO reviews and evidence are on schedule and audit-ready, with no scramble the week before

  • Security questionnaires come back in days, from a library you built, and stop blocking deals

  • The tasks you did by hand in month one are automated, templated, or gone

  • You own things outright that nobody else needs to think about

Logistics

  • Location: London, Old Street (4 days a week in office)

  • Hours: Full time

  • Salary: c.£50,000 depending on experience

  • Reports to: Chief of Staff, who leads operations

description:
Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning
 
Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team—from Finance to HR—to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.

At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo—all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

The Data & Automations Team

The Data & Automations team builds and operates Pigment's internal data platform, and designs, implements, and maintains the intelligent automation solutions that rely on it. Together, they streamline business processes and enhance data-driven decision making: we empower product, business and corporate functions through technology integration, robust data architecture, and process optimization, enabling teams to focus on high-value activities while ensuring accuracy and scalability.

The data platform is the foundation of everything we deliver. It is a centralized, governed ecosystem that collects, stores, transforms, and serves data to internal consumers across Product, Go-To-Market (GTM), and General & Administrative (G&A) functions, providing a single source of truth for analytics, automations, and AI. Making it reliable, secure, cost-efficient, and scalable is at the core of our mission. The team also consolidates and orchestrates AI efforts across Pigment, from governance and enablement to building AI-powered solutions.

Our team tackles diverse challenges, from integrating finance and HR systems and streamlining employee lifecycle processes, to building pipelines that turn product usage and customer interactions into actionable insights for Finance or GTM teams. AI is now at the center of most of what we do with data: many of our pipelines feed LLM-powered solutions, and the quality, structure, and governance of our data architecture directly determine what these solutions can deliver.

The team is led by Pigment's Deputy CISO and works closely with the Security team: security and data governance are part of how we build, not an afterthought.

Role

As a Junior Data and Automations Engineer, you will contribute to the continued development of Pigment's data platform: ingestion pipelines, dbt models, orchestration, data quality, and the underlying cloud infrastructure. You will also build and maintain the data pipelines, automations, and AI projects that support our G&A (Finance, People, IT) and GTM (Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships) teams.

You will work closely with senior engineers, starting with well-scoped tasks and progressively taking ownership of small projects end to end, from requirements gathering to production monitoring. This role involves collaborating with a wide range of internal stakeholders and requires excellent communication skills in English (primarily) and French, verbal and written.

Tech environment

Our core stack relies on Google Cloud Platform, maintained with Terraform, with components including BigQuery, Cloud Run, and Cloud Composer (Airflow), as well as dbt, Fivetran, Hightouch, Elementary for data observability, and Python for integrations and automations. Our pipelines connect business systems such as Salesforce, NetSuite, our HRIS, Gong, or Slack, and feed Pigment applications used by our own business teams. You will have the opportunity to learn and grow your skills across these technologies while making a meaningful impact on Pigment's operational efficiency.

Data Platform & Infrastructure:

  • Build and maintain dbt models that turn raw data into clean, documented, and tested datasets
  • Contribute to the evolution of our orchestration, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code setup
  • Help improve data quality, observability, and alerting across the platform

  • Build pipelines and integrations that sync data between business systems (CRM, ERP, HRIS) through our data warehouse, including reverse ETL with Hightouch
  • Develop Python-based automations that remove manual work for teams such as Finance, People, IT, and Customer Success

Monitoring & Support:

  • Document data models, pipelines, and processes for both technical and business readers

Collaboration & Learning:

About Nabla

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

About the Role

We are scaling our healthcare AI platform, with more products, integrations and AI agents, and more protected health information (PHI) flowing through them. To keep pace, we're growing our security engineering team and looking for an exceptional Senior Security Engineer.

Our cloud infrastructure handles highly sensitive healthcare data, so security is core to everything we do. Our engineers already ask the right questions every day: can we use a one-time token here? How long should it live? How do we scope this OAuth Client?

You'll work directly with our Lead Security Engineer to bring real AppSec expertise into the product squads, and to strengthen security well beyond them.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role. About half your time goes to AppSec, but it is deliberately a broad security engineering role, not a pure code-review or pentest job. You'll regularly cross into platform and cloud, CI/CD and detection, and you'll own problems from start to finish. Code scanning, SCA and AI-driven code review are already running, but there is no AppSec process to undo. The threat-modeling practice, the security review loop, the triage rhythm and the secure-by-default libraries don't exist yet. You'll build them and run them.

If you're pragmatic, love working shoulder to shoulder with developers, and want your work to protect patients' most sensitive data, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the product squads as their go-to security engineer: design reviews, per-feature threat modeling, and fast, opinionated answers on authN/authZ, tokens and session design.

  • Secure our authentication and authorization surfaces (OAuth clients, one-time codes, multi-org tenancy, the Core API user API, embedded/postMessage SDKs) and hunt for BOLA, IDOR and broken access control before attackers do.

  • Run the code-security findings loop: triage and prioritize results from our SAST, SCA, secrets and IaC scanners and AI-driven code review, route them to the right owners with SLAs, and drive the dependency-vulnerability backlog down, fixing issues yourself when that's faster.

  • Secure our AI/LLM features and internal agents, covering prompt injection, tool and permission scoping for autonomous agents, PHI leakage, de-identification assurance and model/API egress.

  • Run the external testing program: scope and run pentests (web, mobile, backoffice), validate fixes, operate our vulnerability disclosure program, and stand up a bug bounty.

  • Build secure-by-default guardrails (secure coding guidelines, hardened libraries and patterns, pre-commit and PR checks) so the secure path is the easy path.

Qualifications

  • 5 to 8+ years in security engineering, including at least 2 to 3 years in application or product security, or experience as a software engineer with a strong security focus.

  • Deep understanding of modern web and API security: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, session and token design, multi-tenancy, and the OWASP Top 10 and API Top 10. You can find access-control flaws by reading code.

  • Strong coder, comfortable reading and fixing production code (mostly Kotlin and Python, plus web, mobile and desktop clients) and automating in Python.

  • Experience running threat modeling and security design reviews, and operating SAST, SCA and secrets scanning in CI with a real triage loop, not just a dashboard.

  • Genuine breadth: comfortable moving between an API design review, a supply-chain hardening PR and an incident in the same week, and honest about what you don't know yet.

  • Excellent communicator who earns developers' trust and works well with engineering, compliance and IT.

  • Full professional fluency in French and English (oral and written).

Nice to have: LLM / AI agent security, mobile app security, pentest or bug bounty experience, GCP / GKE, or experience in healthcare or another regulated industry.

Life at Nabla

When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed.

  • Multi-jurisdiction financial complexity: hands-on experience with transfer pricing, intercompany structures, and multi-party revenue recognition across at least two of the following: Europe, the US, and Asia.

title: Senior Sales Manager - Media (m/w/d)
Frontend Engineer - Agentic AI
description:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Your Mission

As a Frontend Engineer at Hawk, you will build and maintain the user interface of our agentic AI Investigation Agent. This is the product where compliance analysts configure AI workflows, watch autonomous investigations run, and review, question and act on what the agent concludes.

The frontend is a modern TypeScript monorepo made of a host application and a growing set of independently deployable microfrontends. These remotes are designed to be built once and used in two places: our new shadcn/ui-based Investigation Agent and our existing Material UI-based Case Manager. Your job is to understand this codebase deeply, keep it healthy, and ship new features with care, from the component level all the way to how it is built and deployed.

What You'll Work On:

  • Features: Build product features end to end in React and TypeScript, such as workflow graph editors, investigation timelines, data-heavy tables and dashboards that make agentic AI output understandable for analysts.

  • Microfrontends: Develop and maintain Module Federation remotes, keep remote/host contracts stable, and make sure features fit into both the Investigation Agent and the MUI-based Case Manager.

  • Design system and data layer: Contribute to our shared shadcn/ui + Tailwind component library (documented in Storybook), and consume our Python/FastAPI backends through OpenAPI-generated clients with TanStack Query and Router.

  • Build, test and deploy: Work in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with GitHub Actions CI, Vitest and Playwright tests, and deployments to AWS including per-PR preview environments.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with Product, UX, backend engineers and Data Science, and use AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor as part of your everyday workflow.

Your Profile:

  • 3–5 years building and maintaining production React applications, with strong TypeScript and modern React skills (hooks, composition, performance, complex state and forms).

  • Clean frontend architecture: you structure code around features and clear boundaries. You keep UI components presentational and reusable, put data fetching and business logic in hooks and typed API layers, and keep server state separate from local UI state. You prefer composition, small focused components and strict typing, and you treat cross-module contracts as an API.

  • Design-system experience: hands-on work with a component-library approach, ideally shadcn/ui, Radix and Tailwind. Familiarity with Material UI is a strong plus.

  • Microfrontends and delivery: Module Federation or similar runtime composition, shared dependencies and host/remote contracts, plus the build and deployment basics behind them: Vite, monorepos (pnpm workspaces, Turborepo or Nx), CI pipelines (GitHub Actions)

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you're happy working on problems that aren't fully defined yet. You ask the right questions, make sensible assumptions, build a first version and refine it with Product and UX, without waiting for a perfect spec.

  • AI tooling: daily, practical use of AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.).

  • Communication: clear communication in English, and the ability to explain technical decisions to both technical and non-technical colleagues.

Bonus:

  • Some Python: enough to read a FastAPI endpoint or Pydantic model, run the backend locally, trace a bug across the API boundary, or open a small backend PR. You don't need to be a backend engineer.

  • Infrastructure as code: exposure to Terraform or AWS CDK.

  • Quality tooling: Storybook-driven development, visual regression testing or accessibility testing.

  • Auth: Auth0/OIDC integration in single-page apps.

  • Domain interest: UX for AI products, or previous work in fintech, RegTech or compliance.

title: Senior Associate, Internal Communications, International
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Company

DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt are one global team building the future of local commerce. Our products power millions of interactions between consumers, merchants, and couriers every day, in cities around the world. Together, we're combining global scale with deep local understanding to deliver what's next. In this role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across all three brands.

About the Team

This role sits within the Global Internal Communications team, a high-impact group focused on engaging and connecting with DoordDash, Deliveroo and Wolt's most important audience: our employees. This role will specifically support the International business (Deliveroo and Wolt) in Europe and the Middle East (EMEA).

We are responsible for leading employee communications centred around our company-wide strategy, business goals, and financial results to ensure employees understand the company's near- and long-term vision. This team works cross-functionally with key business stakeholders, touching every corner of the organisation.

About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Manager, International Internal Communications, you will provide support across the Deliveroo and Wolt businesses including being the key internal comms point of contact for our EMEA country teams, working on change and issues communications, and partnering on content creation and relevant internationally focused projects. 

This role is ideal for someone with between 5-10 years of communications experience who is experienced in working with multiple stakeholders in fast paced but sometimes ambiguous environments. You will partner closely with the Senior Manager to translate complex or evolving information into clear, effective communications for employees.

Day to day you'll be:

  • Acting as the main internal comms point of contact for Deliveroo and Wolt (EMEA) country teams and regional communications managers

  • Building and maintaining the community of internal communicators across the EMEA footprint, sharing best practice and editorial guidance and keeping consistency with international IC standards.

  • Supporting crisis and issues communications across EMEA, partnering with the Senior Director and Senior Managers 

  • Providing change management comms support, partnering with the change management comms lead and people team on delivery.

  • Creating content to support company level events, such as all hands

  • Leading on analytics and measurement for such events for the international internal comms team, working closely with the digital channels team.

  • Operating effectively as part of a global team partnering with the international business.

We're excited about you because…

  • You have a strong (5yrs +) track record of communications experience.

  • You work well with multiple stakeholders across countries and brands, and can build and sustain a network of communicators.

  • You thrive in fast paced, sometimes ambiguous environments, and stay effective when situations move quickly.

  • You can translate complex or evolving information into clear, effective communications for employees.

  • You are comfortable supporting crisis, issues and change communications.

  • You are comfortable with data, and can turn engagement reporting into insights.

  • You are flexible and can turn your hand to a wide range of comms projects and topics  

Next steps

  • Step 1: Apply before Mon 26th October

  • Step 2: Screening with our recruitment team

  • Step 3: Panel interview with hiring manager and team lead

  • Step 4: Written test and final interview

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: Cybersecurity Project Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Who are we?

It all starts with the mission: NVISO is here to protect European society from potentially devastating cyber attacks. This means we offer cyber security services to private and governmental organizations to help them better prepare for, prevent, detect and respond to cyber security incidents. All of this is built on four fundamental values that define who we are: We are Proud, We Break Barriers, We Care and No BS!

What will you do?

As Cybersecurity Project Manager (m/w/d) based in Germany, you will lead the delivery of projects that help protect organisations and the people who depend on them across Europe. You will bring together NVISO specialists in security operations, automation, Detection Engineering, Cybersecurity Architecture and incident response to turn customer ambitions into delivered security solutions.

You will manage implementation, integration and improvement projects from kick-off through acceptance and handover to the teams responsible for ongoing operations. You will keep scope, timelines and dependencies aligned, and make sure customers and colleagues know what has been agreed, what comes next and where a decision is needed.

You will work closely with Business Development, senior management and technical experts, organising their contributions and following commitments through. Your cybersecurity knowledge will help you ask informed questions and connect technical dependencies to delivery decisions. Experts retain technical ownership; you bring the people, plans and decisions together to deliver the project.

Typical responsibilities include:

· Managing implementation projects from kick-off to acceptance, with clear scope, milestones, dependencies and responsibilities across NVISO teams and customer stakeholders;

· Securing commitments from capability leads and organising timely support and decisions from Business Development, senior management and technical experts;

· Leading customer meetings and delivery reporting, aligning expectations and communicating progress, risks and next steps in language suited to each audience;

· Managing risks, issues and scope changes, agreeing achievable plans and escalating decisions with clear options and their impact on delivery;

· Tracking effort, budget consumption and forecast-to-complete, and reporting deviations and proposed actions to the senior manager, who retains P&L ownership;

· Coordinating expert validation, customer acceptance and operational handover, then closing the project with follow-up actions assigned and lessons captured.

What we are looking for

  • You hold citizenship in one of the 32 NATO member states or the Austrian citizenship;

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent professional experience;

  • Experience managing multi-team cybersecurity or IT implementation projects, covering planning, dependencies, risks, scope changes and delivery reporting;

  • Sound understanding of security operations, detection and response, automation and cybersecurity architecture, sufficient to discuss dependencies with experts and explain their delivery implications;

  • Experience tracking effort, budgets and forecasts, and coordinating contributors and decisions across several teams without direct line-management authority;

  • Experience in consulting or customer-facing delivery is an advantage; a project management qualification such as PMP or PRINCE2 is welcome;

  • Fluent business English and professional fluency in German (at least C1-level).

Your benefits

Within the Face team, we develop systems for face verification, uniqueness and duplicate detection, presentation attack detection, and supporting capabilities such as face detection, image quality assessment, occlusion detection, pose estimation, and others that allow these systems to operate reliably in real-world conditions.

Our work spans the full machine learning lifecycle: defining data-collection and labeling requirements, curating datasets, conducting applied computer-vision research, training and evaluating models, adversarial testing, supporting deployment, investigating production behavior, and monitoring performance after release.

The problems we work on are grounded in real-world conditions. Our systems must handle variation in cameras, lighting, pose, image quality, occlusion, user behavior, and attack methods. They must also operate within strict latency and memory budgets and interact with privacy-preserving systems (Anonymized Multi-Party Computation) that compare users against a growing identity set. At our scale, small regressions can have a meaningful impact, so evaluation, operating-point selection, and production monitoring are central to how we work.

We are pragmatic about our methods. We use deep learning where it provides clear value, classical computer vision and image processing where they are more efficient or reliable, and hybrid approaches when they produce the best system.

Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We’re looking for a doctor who has moved into AI and can code, to join Clinical AI R&D as a Clinical AI Engineer. You’ll sit inside a product pod and own the evidence for its product: define the evaluation before anyone builds, run it to a standard a journal reviewer would accept, keep watching the product once it ships, publish what the evidence shows, and change the product when the evidence says to.



The pod’s engineers can change the product but can’t judge whether a discharge summary missed something a consultant would catch. Clinicians can make that call but can’t open a pull request. You do both, and you treat the gap between a model’s output and good clinical practice as the thing you’re here to measure and close.



The loop doesn’t end at launch. You stay with the product for its life in market.

 

What you’ll do

  • Design the evaluation. Define evaluations for greenfield products to an academic standard: endpoints, comparators, ground truth, sample size, analysis plan. Set the bar before the result arrives.

  • Build the measurement. Build, optimize and validate the LLM judges and rubrics that score the product at scale. Report their agreement with clinician ground truth, not their convenience, and retire the ones that drift.

  • Run it and write it up. Execute the evaluation, do the statistics, and write it up once in a form that serves the pod, the regulatory file and an academic submission.

  • Run post-market surveillance. Monitor output quality in production and respond to regulatory feedback with data. Our clinical safety team triages complaints and incidents; you’re their counterpart in the pod, working out what their findings mean for the product and what should change.

  • Fix what the evidence finds. Prompt and rubric changes, evaluation harness changes, code changes in the pod’s codebase, shipped through the pod’s normal review and release process.

  • Publish. Contribute to peer-reviewed literature on the translational benefit of the product.

  • Be the clinician in the room. Catch the output that reads well and is wrong. Hold the line on clinical nuance when a shortcut would ship faster.

 

What you'll need

  • A medical degree and clinical practice with independent clinical judgment. This role runs on medical nuance, and this requirement doesn’t flex.

  • Academic depth. Study design, inferential statistics, agreement and reliability measures, sample size, handling of multiple comparisons. Thesis or publication-level work, not a methods module.

  • Experience evaluating medical software or clinical AI, including building or validating LLM-as-judge pipelines.

  • Enough engineering to work in a production codebase. Read it, understand what a change will do, make the change in Python or TypeScript, and get it through review. Prompt engineering and AI-assisted coding are daily tools here, and they’re the floor, not the ceiling.

  • Independence. You can run a project for weeks with light direction, and you say early when it’s stuck.

  • Clear writing. Evaluation reports, surveillance summaries and manuscripts are the primary output of this role.

Nice to have

  • Post-market surveillance or vigilance work under a medical device framework (TGA, MHRA, FDA or EU MDR). Appetite to learn counts for more than existing depth.

  • Peer-reviewed publications on clinical AI or LLM evaluation.

  • Machine learning background beyond prompting, such as fine-tuning or classical model evaluation.

  • Specialty depth in an area Heidi is moving into.

  • An academic or clinical-site network able to host a study.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

title: Senior HW Engineer – PCB Layout
description:
The Opportunity

Lumai's optical engine only works if the electronics around it hold up. Our boards carry large FPGAs and custom ASICs, multi-gigabit links and fine-pitch packages, and they have to be laid out to tolerances that leave no room for guesswork. This role takes the designs coming out of our hardware and SI/PI teams and turns them into manufacturable, high-layer-count boards.

The Role

You will own board layout from schematic handoff to fabrication release. That covers stackups and HDI structures, controlled-impedance routing, differential pairs, length and phase matching, BGA breakout for large fine-pitch devices, and the full manufacturing package: Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings and fabrication notes. You will also own the footprint and symbol libraries, the design rules and the CAD standards the rest of the team works to.

What is genuinely hard about it is that the constraints are real and they conflict. Signal integrity, power integrity, thermal and mechanical requirements all land on the same square centimetres, and the fabricator's process limits decide what is actually buildable. You will be the person who turns simulation output into layout rules and who can defend a stackup to a fabricator.

By month six, you will have taken at least one board through to fabrication release, set the libraries and design rules the team works from, and be the first point of contact for our fabricators and assembly houses.

What You'll Do

  • Lay out dense, high-layer-count PCBs from schematic through to fabrication release, using constraint-driven flows.

  • Implement controlled-impedance routing, differential pair and length/phase matching, and HDI structures including microvias, via-in-pad and back-drilling.

  • Plan BGA breakout and component placement for large FPGAs, custom ASICs and fine-pitch packages, balancing SI, PI, thermal and mechanical requirements.

  • Translate SI/PI and hardware constraints into layout rules, and iterate quickly with engineers on simulation feedback.

  • Run DFM, DFA and DFT reviews, and act as the main technical contact with PCB fabricators and assembly houses.

  • Generate complete manufacturing outputs (Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings, fabrication notes) and manage design revisions.

  • Own and maintain the footprint and symbol libraries, CAD standards and design templates, compliant with IPC standards.

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • Extensive professional experience laying out complex, high-speed, high-layer-count boards, with a portfolio of designs that went into production.

  • Expert proficiency in Cadence Allegro, including Constraint Manager. Equivalent Altium experience will also be considered.

  • Hands-on experience with HDI technologies: microvias, via-in-pad, stacked and staggered vias, and back-drilling.

  • Proven BGA breakout and placement for large, fine-pitch devices such as FPGAs and ASICs.

  • Thorough working knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-6012) and of DFM/DFA/DFT principles.

Strong preference for

  • Boards carrying 56G+ SerDes, PCIe Gen5/6 or DDR5 interfaces.

  • Working closely with SI/PI simulation engineers.

  • Rigid-flex, RF or mixed-signal layouts.

  • ECAD/MCAD collaboration on thermal and mechanical integration.

  • Experience setting up CAD standards, libraries and design templates in a growing team.

About Lumai

Lumai is the optical compute company building the next generation of AI infrastructure. Spun out of optics research at the University of Oxford in 2021, we compute with light instead of electrons. Our 3D optical technology carries out the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inside beams of light travelling through free space, which lets it go beyond the limits of both silicon GPUs and integrated photonics.

In April 2026 we launched Iris Nova, the world's first optical computing system to run billion-parameter large language models in real time, using up to 90% less energy than conventional GPU-based systems. Iris Nova, the first server in the family, is now available for evaluation by hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises and research institutions. Aura and Tetra will follow.

Our work won the Falling Walls Award for Science Breakthrough of the Year 2025 and 'Best Overall Technology' at the OCP Future Technologies Symposium. We are headquartered in Oxford.

Why Lumai

You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec.

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. The mission of our 270 collaborators is to help brands transform customer and employee experiences through tailored insights, strategy, and implementation.

We are passionate about delivering impact.

Our clients include the world's most admired luxury houses, and our solutions combine research, technology, and human expertise to elevate every customer interaction.

We are looking for a thought leadership expert with the editorial vision to spot what matters next, the conviction to shape CXG's point of view, and the writing talent to make it influential across luxury retail, beauty and cosmetics, watches and jewellery, automotive, and hospitality.

Context and role

Reporting to the Chief of Staff, you will lead CXG's Thought Leadership and Market Intelligence functions. You will define the topics on which CXG should have a distinctive and credible point of view, turn CXG's proprietary data, expertise and market knowledge into original external content, and position the company ahead of emerging developments in customer experience, luxury and its priority verticals.

This is a hands-on role: you will research, analyse, write and produce content yourself, while mobilising expertise and data from across the business. You will be accountable for ensuring that every publication presents a recognisable CXG angle rather than simply reporting market developments or repeating established industry views. You will manage one Market Intelligence team member.

Thought Leadership Development

  • Define the thought leadership strategy and roadmap, including priority themes, target audiences, formats and a realistic publication calendar.
  • Drive and coordinate content creation across Practices, Solutions and Regions.
  • Work closely with Practices, Regions and Solutions to:
    • Push: scan for trends and hot topics and ensure CXG has a voice and perspective, commenting regularly on these subjects.
    • Pull: identify and collect new ideas and proposed topics from the relevant stakeholders, prioritise and incorporate them into the thought leadership roadmap.
  • Use market intelligence, CXG's proprietary data, internal expertise and client-facing insights to identify emerging topics early, develop a clear CXG point of view and decide where CXG can make a credible contribution to the conversation.
  • Research, interview internal experts, write and edit articles, perspectives and other thought leadership content directly. Challenge generic claims and ensure each piece advances a clear argument and is supported by credible evidence.
  • Ensure that analysis is methodologically sound, appropriately contextualised and presented without compromising client confidentiality.
  • Develop topics that connect expertise across Practices and Regions, while reflecting relevant differences between markets.

Thought Leadership Communication

  • Ensure relevant thought leadership pieces (e.g., perspectives, publications) are disseminated on a periodic basis.
  • Work with Marketing on the publication, distribution and promotion of content, while retaining ownership of the editorial strategy, substance, quality and consistency of CXG's point of view. In addition, collaborate with Marketing to maximise impact by communicating through the channels relevant to each market.
  • Track the reach, engagement and qualitative response generated by CXG's thought leadership, as well as relevant business enquiries influenced by published content. Use the findings to refine the roadmap.
  • Shape and host or contribute to CXG's podcast "The Luxury Edit", working with internal experts and guests to develop topics, prepare interviews and turn conversations into useful content.
  • Develop the content and key messages for CXG-hosted events and external conferences, panels and talks; act as a CXG speaker where appropriate; and work with internal experts to prepare other CXG speakers and turn the company's point of view into compelling presentations and discussion topics.
  • Look for and test new thought leadership formats (e.g., interactive reports, data visualisations, short-form video, newsletters, social-first content) to broaden reach, engage new audiences and keep CXG's content distinctive.
  • Identify and build collaborations with conferences, specialised industry magazines and universities (e.g., content partnerships, guest articles, co-branded publications, joint research, guest lectures, speaking slots) to extend CXG's visibility and credibility with target audiences.

Market Intelligence

  • Keep abreast of market and competitive developments and ensure relevant findings are communicated across CXG.
  • Translate these findings into clear implications for CXG's strategic priorities, client conversations, commercial opportunities and external thought leadership.
  • Contribute market intelligence, evidence and relevant CXG perspectives to priority proposals and client deliverables, working with Practices, Solutions and Regions to strengthen the quality and relevance of the final output.
  • Manage and develop the Market Intelligence team member, setting clear priorities and reviewing the quality and usefulness of their work.

  • Identify gaps in the conversations competitors are leading and opportunities for CXG to establish a distinct position.

Industry Analysis

  • Research and review clients' developments (e.g., new strategy, launch of new product or service, restructuring, M&A, key managerial appointments).
  • Track public financial announcements (e.g., quarterly and annual earnings).
  • Monitor developments in luxury, retail, customer experience and adjacent sectors; distinguish lasting shifts from short-lived topics and explain their implications for CXG and its clients.
  • Publish the weekly "This Week in Luxury" news brief and issue timely flash updates when significant developments require immediate attention, such as financial announcements, major transactions or leadership changes.

title: Head of Security
description:
About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

 

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.

Location:

Paris or remote (from -5h GMT up to +2h GMT to ensure sufficient overlap with the rest of the team).

About the role:

As Head of Security, you'll define and drive Morpho's security strategy across the entire organization - corporate IT, cloud and infrastructure, application, supply chain, identity, incident response, threat intelligence, and counterparty security - and you'll build the team and function to deliver it. This is a hands-on leadership role: in the early days you'll personally do the work while you hire, and you'll stay close enough to the technical detail to earn the trust of a deeply technical organization. You'll also be Morpho's credible security voice, internally to leadership, and externally to the integrators, institutions, and ecosystem partners who depend on us. You'll partner closely with Engineering on infrastructure and deployment integrity, and with our Integration team, which works with various partners across the Morpho ecosystem.

Responsibilities:

  • Own and continuously evolve Morpho's security strategy and roadmap across, cloud/infrastructure, application, supply-chain, identity, and operational security.

  • Build and lead the security function - hire, grow, and develop the team, recruiting skillsets across security operations and application security.

  • Oversight of the IT function

  • Stay hands-on. Personally execute critical security work - threat modeling, architecture review, control implementation, and incident command - while the team scales.

  • Set the governance architecture: a coherent security framework that ties tooling and controls together, rather than accumulating tools in isolation.

  • Own incident response end to end - runbooks, incident command, severity and escalation structure, and market communication during an event.

  • Build and run a counterparty security program for curators and partners - identity verification, screening, operational diligence, and bidirectional incident-coordination channels.

  • Lead Morpho's certification strategy (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001), meeting both the spirit and the letter sustainably.

  • Represent Morpho's security posture externally - to fintechs, financial institutions, and the broader ecosystem - and internally to executives.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Engineering, Protocol, and Integrations, driving security outcomes through both direct ownership and influence.

What Success Looks Like:

First 30 Days

  • You've built a clear, independent picture of Morpho's posture, architecture, threat model, and in-flight work - and pressure-tested the existing strategy against it.

  • You've met the team and established working relationships with the people who own the surfaces you'll most depend on.

  • You understand the path-to-funds attack surface in depth and have an early, evidence-based view of the highest-severity risks and quick wins.

  • You know exactly where incident-response readiness stands today.

First 60 Days

  • You've published a clearly prioritized security roadmap with clear sequencing, owners, and the rationale for what's deferred and aligned leadership behind it.

  • You've defined the team build-out plan and opened the first hire.

  • You're personally driving the top-severity gaps - identity and authentication enforcement, deployment guardrails, and a documented incident-response runbook among them.

  • You've set the governance framework and the certification path in motion.

First 90 Days

  • Demonstrable progress closing the highest-priority gaps, with key controls enforced rather than optional.

  • A documented incident-response capability that's been validated by at least one tabletop exercise.

  • Hiring underway, and a clear operating rhythm established with Engineering, Protocol, and Integrations.

  • Morpho's external security posture is taking shape - trust surface, counterparty security program, and ecosystem engagement - and you're recognized internally and externally as Morpho's credible security voice.

Must-have Experience & Skills:

  • 10+ years in security, several of them building or leading a security function, ideally at a crypto/web3, fintech, or financial-services company where security is core to the business.

  • Strong grasp of the crypto/web3 threat model

  • Proven experience building and growing a security team from a small base, recruiting across security operations and application/infrastructure security.

  • Deep, hands-on technical expertise across cloud, infrastructure, CI/CD, supply-chain, identity, and application security - you do the work, not just direct it.

  • Owned incident response end to end, including incident command and external communication.

  • Sharp prioritization and the ability to galvanize action through hard and soft influence, including driving outcomes through teams you don't own.

  • Exceptional, organized, responsive communication - credible to executives and to external audiences from fintechs to Fortune 500 institutions.

  • Humble.

Nice to Have:

  • An established network and public profile in the security or crypto-security community, and comfort representing security work publicly (talks, writing, framework contribution).

  • Offensive security depth, or experience standing up red/blue capabilities.

  • Familiarity with institutional and regulatory expectations and threat-sharing networks (e.g. Crypto ISAC, TIBER-style frameworks).

  • Taken an organization through certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent)

Perks & Benefits

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

 

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.

As we scale, we're splitting Finance into three specialized poles: FP&A, Finance Operations (Financial Control & Accounting), and Procurement. This role anchors Finance Operations (Financial Control & Accounting) — the pole that keeps Joko's financial information accurate, timely, and audit-ready. You'll report directly to Quentin, our COO.

 

✨ Why this role is special

Finance Operations (Financial Control & Accounting) is a brand-new specialized pole at Joko — previously bundled into a single generalist Finance Manager role. You'll be the first person to own this scope end to end, with direct visibility to the COO and VP Finance with real influence over how the function is built as the company scales past 200 people across multiple geographies.

  • Lead our international accounting build-out: as we open new entities and markets, including our IFRS consolidation framework;

  • Own cash management: reconciliation, yield optimization, and day-to-day treasury;

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: 4–8 years, with a strong foundation in accounting or audit (Big 4 or equivalent), ideally combined with in-house experience in a scale-up.

  • Education: A master's degree from a top business school. A double degree in accounting (DCG/DSCG) is a plus.

  • International mindset: Excited to build a multi-entity, multi-country accounting backbone as we expand; IFRS exposure is a plus.

  • Problem solving: You dig into the root cause and fix things.

  • Languages: Fluent French and English.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

description:
The Senior Machine Learning Engineer, ML Platform is responsible for building, running, and evolving the ML monorepo used by the X-ray, CT, and MRI machine learning group at DeepHealth. The monorepo covers the full path from experimentation to product: dataset and sample definitions, training and evaluation code, experiment tracking, model export, and the inference servers that run in production. Everyone on the team contributes to the monorepo; this role is the single point of accountability for it. This hands-on role owns the architecture, tooling, and engineering standards of that codebase for a distributed team of about twenty machine learning engineers and scientists, working with model developers and software engineers to make the team’s work fast, better, and easier to audit. It also leads the team's agentic coding strategy, shaping how AI coding agents are used across the codebase. The role reports to the Leader of the ML for X-ray/CT/MRI group.

  • Build and run the engineering tooling around the codebase:

    • Continuous integration, testing, dependency management, containers, artifact and model registries, and GPU job scheduling on cloud (GCP) and HPC infrastructure.

  • Own the path from trained checkpoint to deployable model:

    • Model packaging, inference servers with enforced API contracts, reproducibility, and performance and memory budgets on target hardware.

  • Define and enforce engineering standards (code review, testing, documentation) in a way that accelerates research rather than slowing it down.

  • Ensure traceability of data, code, and model versions across experiments and releases.

  • Investigate and resolve performance, reliability, and usability issues in the stack raised by the team and reduce their recurrence through shared tooling.

  • Drive the team's agentic coding strategy: define how AI coding agents are used in the monorepo, set up the tooling, guardrails, and conventions that make them effective, and help colleagues adopt them.

title: Founding Product Builder
description:
If you think product management means writing tickets for engineers to execute, this role isn't for you.
If you think AI is a feature you bolt onto a roadmap after the fact, this role isn't for you either.

---

We believe AI doesn't create talent. It amplifies it.
Used poorly, it generates an exponential amount of technical debt.
Used well, it becomes a team of eager junior engineers capable of executing at machine speed.
The quality of the outcome depends on how well you organize them, guide them, and review their work.
---

We're building Lonio, an AI-native backoffice outsourcing service for finance & HR.
Most companies see AI as a product opportunity.
We do too.
But we believe the bigger opportunity lies in execution.
The companies that master AI-native engineering and product development will build faster, learn faster, and out-execute competitors still operating with traditional processes.
That's the company we're building.
This is not an AI product company. This is an AI-native service company.
Want to know how to build it? Watch this.
This is not a classical start-up, we are a spin-off out of BLP Digital, the fastest-growing AI scale-up in Europe.

Tasks

You should be excited by

  • Turning complex Swiss HR and payroll compliance logic into specs engineers can build from without gaps.
  • Owning the product roadmap for our compliance AI automation workflows
  • Working daily with engineering to scope work, sequence what ships next, and catch edge cases before they become technical debt.
  • Joining customer conversations when it sharpens the roadmap. This isn't a GTM role, but you'll sit in on discovery and demo calls often enough to know our customers' problems firsthand.

You'll work directly with Nick (CEO) to translate deep domain knowledge into a product Lauriane (CTO) can execute against.

Requirements

We're less interested in your credentials than your trajectory.
We don't have a predefined model of what a great product person looks like.

What matters to us is that you:

  • Understand what AI agents can and can't reliably do today
  • Write specs precise enough that an engineer builds from them without guessing at edge cases ;)
  • Have strong product fundamentals: prioritization, and turning ambiguity into a plan.
  • Learn fast in a regulated domain you likely don't know yet.
  • Take ownership, including the parts of the job nobody has defined yet.
  • Care about outcomes more than titles.
  • Are comfortable working shoulder to shoulder with engineers daily. This role doesn't stop at strategy and hand off execution.
  • Bonus: German fluency and comfort with Swiss B2B customers (CFOs, Treuhand firms, and payroll specialists), since you'll visit them from time to time.

Benefits

We're flexible on titles, backgrounds, and compensation structures.
If you're unsure whether you qualify, we'd still encourage you to apply.

A final note from the CTO.

Nick knows this domain cold. Swiss payroll compliance, the Treuhand ecosystem, what customers actually need. All of that is in his head.
The hard part is turning that knowledge into specs I can build from without guessing at the edge cases.
That gap is exactly what this role closes.
If you like being the translation layer between deep domain expertise and a small, fast-moving engineering team, you'll enjoy this.

At Machine Learning Architects Basel (MLAB), we assist and empower people and organizations in designing, building, and operating reliable data and machine learning solutions. In doing so, our data and AI journeys and effective solution patterns enable our customers to operationalize, scale, and continuously deliver data and AI products beyond the pilot and prototype stages. These patterns and frameworks revolve not only around the latest technologies but also consider role, skills, and process adjustments. We thereby:

  • Help our customers realize the full potential of data and AI solutions, from use case identification, over data, and ML platform implementation to integration and testing operation of ML models, LLMs, and other GenAI solutions.
  • Design, test, integrate and operate data, model and code pipelines, and end-to-end data/ML/LLM systems (DataOps, MLOps & DevOps).
  • Enable technical and non-technical teams and individuals to leverage data science and management, data, ML, and reliability engineering in an end-to-end fashion.

Aufgaben

Do you want to contribute to our dynamic and growing services company with your Machine Learning, AI, and Software Engineering knowledge? Do you want to act as a thought leader and trusted advisor in the field of Data Products and Data Mesh?

We are looking for a German-speaking Senior Data Engineering Consultant who will be involved in the whole lifecycle of projects, both internally and externally:

  • Consulting, Engineering & Training: You perceive data, software, and AI engineering as key capabilities for mastering the challenges of our clients' digital transformations, want to help them understand both their potential and their limitations, and deliver impactful, valuable services.
  • Requirement Analysis: You analyze customer requirements and identify and define best-fit solutions.
  • Implementation of Data Pipelines and Platforms, ML/LLM Integrations, Reliability Engineering & Operationalization: You understand how to successfully deliver data projects from the prototype or pilot phase into production, design, build, integrate and test data pipelines and platforms, and implement engineering best practices such as traceability, reliability, scalability, measurability, and automation within a demanding project and technology environment.
  • Concept Development: You contribute to our solution blueprints and concepts (e.g., our journey for ‘Reliable Data Products & Efficient Data Meshes’).
  • Expertise & Thought Leadership: You strive to become an expert and a trusted advisor in the field of Data Platforms, Data Products, and DataOps
  • Ownership, Communication, Knowledge Sharing & Teamwork: You take ownership of your work, present your results to various stakeholders, share your knowledge, and collaborate (pro-)actively with our and your client’s teams.

Qualifikation

  • Professional experience (minimum 5 years) as a Data or Software Engineer with a focus on data and ML systems.

  • Experience with and, ideally certified in major data and AI platforms (e.g. Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Azure, MS Fabric).

  • Familiarity with data analytics and DataOps best practices, as well as topics such as Data Mesh, Data Lake/Warehouses, and Reliability Engineering.

  • Understanding and strong interest in the end-to-end life cycle of projects, code, model, and data pipelines, and working with various stakeholders.

  • Technical, hands-on experience with at least some of the following:

  • Programming languages

  • Distributed systems (Hadoop, Spark) and data structures.

  • SQL and NoSQL databases.

  • Cloud Services.

  • REST API and microservices.

  • Docker and knowledge of Kubernetes.

  • Agile development methods and CI/CD.

  • Experience working in a client-facing or consulting role.

  • Fluency in  German and English (written and spoken).

  • Swiss passport or a valid EU/EFTA work permit.

Benefits

  • A young and dynamic services company with an experienced, knowledgeable, and passionate team.
  • An entrepreneurial environment and the chance to have a real impact on the company’s development and growth.
  • Work on cutting-edge data, AI, and analytics topics that have a real impact across industries.
  • A culture that is both performance-oriented and customer-driven and at the same time team-oriented, friendly, and supportive, incl. regular knowledge-sharing sessions and team events
  • A hybrid working model with flexibility as long as both client (of which most require onsite presence) and internal commitments (i.e., one team office day per week) are met.

That's a bigger remit than any one tool. You'll own the CRM data architecture, build the enrichment and signal infrastructure that feeds it, run the integrations and governance holding the wider stack together (Clay, Snowflake, Gong, and more), and build the automations and AI agents that turn all of it into something Marketing, Sales, CS, and BD run on every day. You decide how the whole engine is put together, working across every function rather than waiting inside one for requests.

Where the function stands today

We are building this function from scratch, and therefore you will have the opportunity to lay out the foundations of what a world class AI GTM Engineering team can look like in a fast paced AI company. We are looking for a team that can take and build upon the existing state- Marketing has built real foundation where enrichment runs steadily, AI nurturing agents are live and lifting reply rates, intent signals flow in from across the funnel, and HubSpot is trusted as the data model of record for accounts, contacts, deals, and lifecycle stages.

Beyond that, there's a funnel zone each for Sales, CS, and BD still waiting to be built out, on top of the intelligence Marketing already relies on.

We need operators who are instinctively drawn to turning manual process into clean systems, and ungoverned data into governed infrastructure. People who've spent their growth, marketing, sales, or RevOps careers quietly building automations and tightening the infrastructure underneath their own work, and are ready to do both full-time inside a function that already has shape and runway.

What you will be doing

CRM & data architecture

  • Administer and evolve the HubSpot data model: accounts, contacts, deals, and lifecycle stages.

  • Implement lead routing, ICP, and territory logic into the CRM per rules RevOps defines - you build it, RevOps owns what it means.

  • Implement rules of engagement (ROE) - handoff criteria and account rules - into CRM workflows, automation, and Clay infrastructure that execute them reliably.

  • Build and maintain enrichment via Clay and providers such as ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit, and Starbridge.

  • Run TAM analysis and intent-data infrastructure, and keep data quality high through continuous enrichment workflows.

  • Decide which signals matter, how to surface them, and how to route them to the people who should act on them.

  • Own GTM tool integrations end to end (Gong, Snowflake, Clay, Default AI, Starbridge, dialers, Common Room, or equivalent) so data flows cleanly with no duplicate or conflicting records.

  • Apply data governance standards: review automation that touches shared CRM objects, and respect change control on the data model.

  • Shape vendor and tool decisions - fit, overlap, integration complexity - so we consolidate instead of running five tools for one job.

Automation & AI build

  • Build and maintain the core Clay & Lemlist infrastructure: account data, enrichment, sequences, templates, and how contacts flow in and out.

  • Develop account scoring models and standardized Clay functions that Sales and Marketing can use without building their own underlying workflows.

  • Build agents, automations, and AI-assisted workflows in Claude, Default AI, and connected tooling.

Activate the build across every funnel zone

  • Marketing (inbound signal → MQL): inbound enrichment and routing, audience activation, intent signal infrastructure. Drive signal-based outbound - detect a buying moment (hiring, funding, leadership change, product usage shift), find the decision-maker, enrich, send.

  • Sales (SQL → Closed Won → Renewal → Expansion): prospecting automation, account planning tooling, rep efficiency. Build lifecycle expansion plays triggered by product signals so CS and AEs get prompted when an account is ready to expand.

  • BD (outbound signal → partner + BD pipeline): partner signal workflows, account intelligence, BD-specific outreach and pipeline automation.

  • CS (Closed Won → Adoption + Health): onboarding automation, health-score workflows, renewal and expansion signal tooling.

Partner with Ops

  • Work through a request → brief → build → feedback model. Ops people are the interface; they translate field needs into precise briefs you execute against.

  • Functions consume what you build rather than configuring or building it themselves, and feedback routes back through Ops - keeping your time focused on builds, not ad hoc asks or slides.

What we're looking for

The mindset matters more than the title on your CV.

  • Comfort owning infrastructure, not just automations. You own a data model, an integration, or a governance rule as confidently as you own the plumbing - not just what sits on top of it.

  • A commercial bias. You ask “does this help close a deal?” before “is this elegant?” You measure your work in meetings booked and pipeline influenced.

  • Cross-functional comfort. You can move between marketing, sales, CS, and engineering languages without losing the room.

Bonus: SQL, Python, or TypeScript. The real signal is willingness to learn by tinkering.

About WeTravel

Passionate travel organizers make this magic happen, and WeTravel is here to support them.

Multi-day travel businesses use WeTravel as their end-to-end operating system: publishing trip offerings, generating and converting leads, processing payments around the world, paying suppliers and vendors. WeTravel helps them grow sales, save time, and save money, so they can focus on delivering incredible bucket-list experiences.

WeTravel is a 400+ person company representing more than 50 countries. We combine global diversity with the agility and closeness of a much smaller team. More than 90 colleagues are based in our Amsterdam office in Rokin, including the entire Product Org and most of our Engineering team.

You will have fun innovating fast with brilliant, low-ego colleagues. Our clients are also easy to reach, which helps us stay close to their needs and build with them.

Financially, WeTravel is highly secure and growing fast, with 50 to 100 percent year-over-year growth depending on the metric. This gives us a strong foundation to build from.

About the Role

This is the domain where our biggest bet is playing out. Building and selling a great multi-day trip is a lot of work: crafting a story worth booking, assembling the content that tells it, and presenting it all in a page a traveler trusts. Our goal is to cut that turnaround down so organizers get back to their client faster, convert more of them, and sell more trips. It also has to hold up as they grow, because a boutique agency selling bespoke trips and a student travel operator running hundreds of departures are building on the same tools. The way we get there is great technology in the hands of organizers and their teams. You will own that end to end, the experience and the engine behind it.

What you'll work on

WeTravel Trips give organizers the tools to create proposals, detailed itineraries and a high-conversion booking experience, while giving them time back to grow and operate their business.

We're now looking for a Staff PM to take this domain through its next phase of growth, and make WeTravel the best software for travel businesses to build, present and sell their trips.

Our success in this domain will drive the growth of our organizers by expanding in several areas:

  • An integrated building experience that helps organizers find the right content and craft the right trip for the right travelers.

  • Shared libraries that pay off most when a team works from them, so every proposal that leaves the company is consistent, beautiful, and unmistakably theirs, whoever wrote it.

  • AI-enabled tools to imagine and create new trips, produce world class content, and optimize their sales funnel.

  • Trip pages organizers can publish and promote wherever their travelers are.

1/ Designing the trip page and selling the trip

Think of the trip page as the product detail page of the travel industry. It is where an organizer's work becomes something a traveler wants, understands, and buys.

  • Dynamic Trip Builder: Intuitive tools for organizers to create their trip offerings, in the languages their travelers read, on WeTravel and beyond it.
